players.product: critical subsystems / weldments & cleaning services for wafer-fab equipment

quarterly_data.signal: Record total revenue of $644.9 million in Q2 2026 compared to $533.7 million in the prior quarter; Products revenue $572.7 million vs $465.7 million last quarter; Services revenue $72.2 million vs $68 million in Q1. Demand increased across both Products and Services as AI-driven investment reshapes semiconductor capital equipment.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $644.9 million (Q1: $533.7 million); Products $572.7 million; Services $72.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: Total gross margin 16.7% vs 16.5% last quarter (Products 15.1% vs 14.6%; Services 28.9% vs 30%); operating margin 7% vs 5.1%; EPS $0.70 on net income of $32.3 million vs $0.31 on $14.5 million in Q1. Operating cash flow was negative $41.1 million on inventory investment to support anticipated demand; cash $255.9 million.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 16.7%; operating margin 7%; EPS $0.70; net income $32.3 million; operating cash flow -$41.1 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: total revenue between $700 million-$750 million and EPS in the range of $0.83-$1.3. Management expects gross margin to move toward the 17% range through the rest of the year, with the goal of 20% gross margin and 10% operating margin at a $4 billion revenue run rate, especially during 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $700 million-$750 million; EPS $0.83-$1.3; target 20% gross margin at $4 billion run rate

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity roadmap: built an additional 26,000 sq ft of clean room space in Malaysia and is increasing capacity within the current footprint in Singapore and the Czech Republic; $3.5 billion capacity ready by end of 2026, matching the current run rate; $4 billion annualized revenue run rate (equivalent to $200 billion WFE) in the first half of 2027. Evaluating a new Southeast Asia expansion (greenfield) to support a $5 billion run rate / $250 billion WFE: capacity beyond $4 billion added in the first half of 2028 and a $5 billion run rate in the second half of 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: 26,000 sq ft clean room added in Malaysia; $3.5 billion capacity by YE2026; $4 billion run rate 1H 2027; $5 billion run rate 2H 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Customers are sharing unprecedented visibility, extending forecasts and giving longer planning horizons; they are booking into the back half of 2027 and some into 2028 (analyst framing) and, being constrained on internal capacity, intend to focus on final test and final integration and overflow subsystem build to partners like UCT, which historically drives Products outgrowth in an upturn.

Biggest customer guided its systems up 30% QoQ for calendar Q3 (analyst); the UCT guide reflects a timing gap between subsystem shipment and customer system integration plus different quarter ends, and aggregated over two quarters UCT revenue growth is on par with or higher than that customer. Top two customers as a percentage of revenue fell from 64 to the high 50s as the customer base diversifies.
quarterly_data.figure: top two customers as percentage of revenue: from the 64 down to the high 50s

quarterly_data.signal: No component shortages or delivery pushouts in Q2 (a competitor reported some): the UCT ramp-readiness campaign secured most critical components well ahead; management expects continued double-digit industry growth quarter by quarter to keep pressure on the WFE supply chain and to produce excursions that must be proactively managed.

WFE outlook: 2026 and 2027 WFE has more deposition and etch intensity; management sees a good chance the industry exceeds $200 billion WFE sometime in 2027 (range $190 billion up to $220 billion) and is preparing for the bull case, with EUV adoption in leading-edge foundry/logic and now memory also growing UCT business with smaller customers.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 WFE $190 billion-$220 billion, chance to exceed $200 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Services expected to grow double digits in 2026 and 2027, with acceleration after the ramp of factories in the U.S., improved utilization at one of its major customers in the U.S., and the planned leading-edge ramp in factories in Korea and Taiwan. Launched the first NPX Center of Excellence in Hillsboro, Oregon for earlier customer engagement on new products.
